# ATTORNEY CALL — QUESTION SHEET

LegalZoom Business Attorney Plan — EULA review call
Tuesday, August 4, 2026 — 12:00 noon ET — 30 minutes
GatewayGuard LLC | William F. Burns III | admin@gatewayguard.co
Dated: 2026-08-04 01:20 ET
Companion to GatewayGuard_License-2026-08-04-0120. Questions 1–8 are in that document's cover note. This sheet covers what to add.

## SAY THIS FIRST — BEFORE ANY QUESTION

The product was renamed. It is now "GatewayGuard Checkup." The July 24 draft called it "the Tool" throughout. The revised license reflects the new name. The copyright registration will be filed as Checkup.
Two cross-references in the July 24 cover note were wrong. The Guide License question pointed to Section 3 — it is Section 5. The liability cap question pointed to Section 7 — it is Section 9. If you reviewed against the wrong sections, those two answers may need revisiting.

## ASK THESE FOUR ON THE CALL

Four questions in thirty minutes is roughly seven minutes each. Do not start further down the list.
9. Are the warranties provable as written? (Section 6)
Two of my five warranties are absolute statements: that "every change is reversible," and that Checkup "makes no network connections from your PC." A single edge case would make either one false. Separate from whether the warranty scope is wise — is the wording provable? Should these be softened, qualified, or moved out of the warranty and into the product description on the website?
Answer:
10. The installed-programs audit feature
A planned feature reviews the programs installed on the user's PC, flags ones we consider risky, and offers to uninstall them with the user's approval. Two exposures: naming a real company's software as risky, and a user removing something they needed. Checkup never removes anything without an on-screen approval, and each approval is logged with a timestamp. Does that design meaningfully limit my exposure, or is the disclaimer doing all the work? Ship at launch, or wait?
Answer:
11. What is missing from this agreement?
The draft has no arbitration clause, no severability clause, no entire-agreement clause, no assignment clause, no age or export restriction, and no mechanism for changing the terms in future versions. For a $19.99 consumer download sold to non-technical home users, which of those do I actually need, and which are unnecessary overhead?
Answer:
12. What am I not asking?
You have read the license and you know the business. What is the largest legal risk in this launch that I have not raised in these twelve questions?
Answer:

## IF TIME REMAINS — OTHERWISE SEND IN WRITING

13. Copyright registration
For source-available software, what goes in the deposit — full source, or the redacted first-and-last-25-pages option? Register as published or unpublished, given it has not launched? Checkup and the Guide as one registration or two? Is registration a prerequisite to suing someone who redistributes the code?
14. Name protection
"GatewayGuard" is the company; "GatewayGuard Checkup" is the product. Is a federal trademark worth filing before there is revenue? Any conflict risk you would check first?
15. Gumroad as merchant of record
If Gumroad is seller of record for the Guide, whose terms bind the buyer — mine or Gumroad's? Does my license still attach to a Gumroad sale?
16. Privacy policy and the hardware fingerprint
Section 2 binds the license to a hardware identifier stored locally on the user's own machine. Does that identifier count as personal data under Maine law or GDPR? Do I need a published privacy policy for a product that collects nothing?
17. Beta tester agreement
Testers get a free license in exchange for running Checkup on their hardware and reporting results. Do I need a separate written agreement, and must it address damage to their machine?
18. Maine sales tax exposure
I am asking Maine Revenue Services directly about registering to collect. I am not asking you to determine taxability — I want to know my exposure if I get it wrong for the first several months, and whether that is a question for you or for a CPA.
19. Incident response
If the signed build is ever tampered with, or the code-signing token is compromised, what am I legally required to do and how quickly? Post-launch guidance is acceptable.

## CALL DISCIPLINE

Ask question 8 last, not first. Question 8 in the cover note asks whether follow-up questions are included or billed separately. The answer tells you whether to send items 13–19 in writing or save them for another consult — so ask it at the end, once you know how much ground you covered.
Do not let question 12 get cut. It is the one that finds risks not already on your list. If the clock is running down, skip 11 and ask 12.
Write answers down during the call, not after. Lines are provided above.

## DECIDE BEFORE THE CALL

Gumroad or your own checkout for Checkup?
Questions 15 and 18 both change answer depending on this. The current plan puts the Guide on Gumroad and Checkup on direct checkout — which is the combination that gives you both sets of obligations at once. Knowing which way you are leaning before noon makes both answers usable.
